significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that "the model's own prior partial-compliance turns" cause most subsequent refusal erosion, with erosion increasing with the model's commitments more than with user-side filler; this is a form-(iii) comparative and dose-response relation backed by a form-(ii) causal decomposition. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon—history-dependent multi-turn refusal decay—and a mechanism separating self-consistency from context dilution, thereby predicting which transcript histories should be dangerous and why "conversational memory hygiene" should work; this directly connects the multi-turn failure documented by The Crescendo Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreak Attack with the refusal-direction mechanism characterized by Arditi et al.'s Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction. Verified false is also informative because it would rule out self-generated concessions as the dominant pathway and redirect explanation toward final-query disguise, generic context dilution, or attack-family-specific mechanisms; the branches are distinguishable through the definite "majority" and "larger than" assertions. In the topic-substitution self-check, generic mechanistic LLM safety would not earn this score: the above-median value comes specifically from attributing a unitary multi-turn failure to two separable pathways and asserting their ordering.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "number/strength of the model's own concessions" as a risk signal and "conversational memory hygiene" as a training-free intervention that masks or re-projects the self-generated concession component. These are ex ante handles because they can flag or neutralize dangerous accumulated history before the model generates the later harmful answer, giving model auditors and deployment engineers an action window rather than merely explaining a completed jailbreak. After per-model re-extraction, the claimed dose-response and ordering—more self-commitment predicts greater refusal erosion than more benign user context—would still predict what should be found across multi-turn attacks, although the submission's explicit caveat that results "may not transfer to frontier models" limits confidence in architecture-wide scope. The topic-substitution self-check does not preserve this score: generic safety interpretability supplies no such forward-looking history signal or inference-time memory rule, whereas this claim would hand both to downstream practitioners.
